newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican cancels media access for Castro audience.
newsitem.headline: Vatican cancels media access for Castro audience.

text.p: The Vatican on Tuesday cancelled all media access for Pope John Paul's long-awaited audience with Cuban President Fidel Castro.
Deputy Vatican spokesman Father Ciro Benedettini told reporters about an hour before the scheduled start of the 11 o'clock (1000 GMT) audience that the usual media arrangements had been cancelled.

Benedettini said the exclusion of the media ensured that the meeting conformed with the protocol of other audiences the Pope held with visiting dignitaries during last week's World Food Summit. Castro arrived in Rome on Saturday.

Some 25 reporters were to have been allowed into the San Damaso courtyard in the Vatican, where heads of state usually alight from their cars and take a lift to the Pope's private library. The audience is expected to last up to an hour.
Under plans announced on Monday, four reporters were due to have acted as a pool inside the library at the end of the private audience.

The Vatican told photographers and television crews on Monday they would be excluded. Only Vatican and Cuban official media will now be allowed to cover the event and the Vatican will hold a briefing for other media later.
